title: [Editor] When upgrading project files, a popup about broken dependencies may appear without clear instructions of what it implies to the process
body:
### Tested versions

4.7.2
4.8.dev (c9730f40aafa4686fa550518c92461258b9ee4b3)

### System information

Windows 10 - Godot Engine v4.8.dev.custom_build.c9730f40a (2026-10-12 14:26:14 UTC) - https://godotengine.org OpenGL API 3.3.0 Core Profile Context 26.8.1.260806 - Compatibility - Using Device: ATI Technologies Inc. - Radeon RX 5500 XT

### Issue description

When you run this tool, the editor restarts, and opens an error popup about the first scene/resource that happened to have dependency issues.

However the process does not wait for dependencies to be fixed, and if there's another scene that needs to resolve issues you will ahve to re-run the upgrade tool to see it

**Why this issue becomes common:** In our team, we have a "playground" folder where any user can throw experimental scenes and resources while working, but those files often become outdated and nobody is really keeping them up to date, so those files become a source of friction when wanting to upgrade the project to latest Godot version.

### Steps to reproduce

- Unzip MRP and run the upgrade tool.
- Every time time you run the tool, you have to solve the issues of only one scene.
- If you dont fix it you cannot see what other scenes has issues too.
- Is also not clear if the process is being interrupted or not.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/065abcc2-f05c-42e4-a3b1-402fd2f41296

### Expected Result
- Dialog should not appear at all during this process. Finding broken dependencies is not the goal of it.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[test-upgrade-issues.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33348214/test-upgrade-issues.zip)

(just in case, i'm also including the project without the missing file)
[test-upgrade-without-issues.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33348219/test-upgrade-without-issues.zip)
